newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 22.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

-The debt-ridden Jinro Group is expected to escape the latest cash-flow crisis as creditor banks agreed to provide rescue loans for the group's key subsidiaries under a cooperative agreement that took effect on Monday.

- Park Kyong-shik, a former presidential family doctor who first divulged the alleged influence-peddling by President Kim Young-sam's son, Hyun-chul, through videotapes, testified on the junior Kim's meddling in state and political affairs at a parliamentary hearing.

- Prosecutors said they will summon former high-ranking intelligence officials, Kim Ki-sup and Oh Jung-so, for questioning over the suspicion they had provided valuable information to Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son.
- The driver and personal aide of Chung Tae-soo, founder of Hanbo group, did not appear at the National Assembly hearing on the Hanbo Scandal. He was scheduled to testify on Monday.
- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko arrived in Seoul on Monday for a three-day visit at the invitation of President Kim Young-sam.
- The South Korean government will allow U.S. intelligence officials to question top North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop, said a senior official at Blue house.
